title: A strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph of the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition
author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph of the Edmonds-Gallai decomposition (author lemma at source lines 1073-1079, label lem:strict-hall). The proof (source lines 1081-1090) is a self-contained matching argument: it extracts, for every vertex v of a component D of the D-part, a maximum matching that leaves v unmatched and therefore has no edge from A into that particular component (proof line 1082), uses the remaining edges to match A into the other components and so obtains a matching saturating A in the graph with one component deleted (proof lines 1083-1085), and then upgrades Hall's inequality to a strict one by noting that equality would break Hall after deleting any neighbour (proof line 1086). The closing count converts the strict inequality into the bound on the number of components of the auxiliary graph (proof lines 1088-1089). The argument is short but every step is used. H2.
